newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WMC says March qtr nickel output rises.
newsitem.headline: WMC says March qtr nickel output rises.

text.p: Mining giant WMC Ltd said on Tuesday it produced 25,768 tonnes of nickel in concentrate in the March quarter, up 6.3 percent from the previous corresponding period.
WMC said stage two of Mount Keith's mill optimisation was commissioned in February which had raised the processing capacity of the operation to 10.5 million tonnes of ore a year.
The company said nickel demand from the stainless steel industry improved in the quarter due to a combination of higher smelting rates by stainless steel mills and lower availability of scrap.

"Supply of nickel appears to be balanced with demand. The average London Metal Exchange (LME) price of nickel increased from US$3.12 per pound in the December quarter to US$3.42 in the March quarter," the company said in its March quarter production report.
WMC said the demand for its smelter grade alumina continued to strengthen during the March quarter as smelter demand increased and metal inventories declined.
This also resulted in improved metal prices and little excess alumina in the market.

"Spot alumina prices have exceeded US$200 per tonne, a substantial improvement over the December quarter, but avaerage alumina prices to Alcoa World Alumina and Chemicals (AWAC) have yet to exceed those in calendar 1996," WMC said.
WMC holds about a 40 percent interest in the AWAC group with is a joint venture with Aluminium Company of America.
Production by the group rose 3.5 percent to 2.5 million tonnes in the March quarter versus the December period, WMC said.
